column11:
In our latest episode of Future of Sports, presented by @adp , Fastbreak AI CEO John Stewart and Chief Product Officer Dr. Chris Groer discuss how artificial intelligence is transforming the business of sports scheduling and league operations.

What once took massive teams, endless spreadsheets, and months of coordination is now becoming faster, smarter, and more efficient through AI-driven technology. From balancing broadcast priorities and travel demands to managing venue conflicts, competitive fairness, and fan experience considerations, scheduling has evolved into one of the most complex operational challenges in professional sports.

Stewart and Groer explain how Fastbreak AI is helping leagues optimize schedules behind the scenes while improving efficiency across organizations. The conversation also explores how AI can support decision-making at scale, reduce operational friction, and unlock new opportunities for leagues navigating increasingly crowded sports calendars.

As sports organizations continue investing in innovation, data, and automation, AI is quickly becoming a critical part of how leagues operate both on and off the field.

column10: The Big Business of Women’s Tennis With WTA’s Sarah Swanson

Swanson shares how her experience helping expand the NFL internationally now informs the WTA’s global strategy, and why women’s tennis continues to outpace its peers in reach, visibility, and commercial value. From leading a major rebrand to securing landmark partnerships, she explains how the WTA is positioning itself at the center of the women’s sports boom.

She also dives into why brands are increasingly prioritizing women’s sports, how athletes are building global platforms, and what the future holds for tennis as a year-round product.

Beyond the headlines, Swanson offers insight into how leagues balance legacy with innovation, from honoring pioneers like Billie Jean King to evolving the fan experience through digital content, storytelling, and new platforms. She also unpacks how the WTA is thinking about player visibility, brand building, and global growth as it looks to define the next era of women’s sports.
